newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent crude races higher on product strength.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent crude races higher on product strength.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures were dragged out of their early doldrums by strong refined product markets, particularly in the United States, brokers said.

Having touched a low of $19.95 per barrel earlier, Oct Brent crude raced up to $20.38 by 1523 GMT, 35 cents up on the day. Brokers said the latest round of U.S. stock data by the American Petroleum Institute, showing falling gasoline stocks and very low distillate inventories, were mostly responsible, despite a sharp rise in crude stocks.
"The APIs were very, very bullish on products. The only thing running us down was crude," said one.

"We are coming into the heating oil season and stocks are very low. And there is going to be great demand for gasoline this weekend," he added, referring to the traditional surge in demand over the U.S. Labour Day holiday on Monday.
A 10 million barrel rise in crude oil stocks last week was countered by falling gasoline and distillate inventories, according to the API data.
Gasoline stocks fell 2.2 million barrels last week to 196.5 million barrels and distillate stocks were 19.3 million barrels below last year.
IPE Sept gas oil rose $2.00 to $191.25 per tonne.
The Oct Brent/gas oil was firm around $5.00 per barrel, from a low of $4.15 on August 19.
